message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred; famed for precision and quality. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Three Michelin stars; intimate setting; renowned for its meticulous preparation. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | Three Michelin stars; focuses on seasonal ingredients and traditional techniques. |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; known for its clean, minimalist style and fresh fish. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular spot for fresh tuna; long lines but worth the wait. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual, open‑air counter; great for a quick, high‑quality bite. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; offers both omakase and set menus. |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Ginza | Known for its creative omakase and excellent service. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; celebrated for its delicate flavors and impeccable presentation. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Shinjuku | Two Michelin stars; offers a refined omakase experience in a cozy setting. |

These restaurants range from high‑end, Michelin‑starred establishments to more casual yet still top‑quality spots. Reservations are often required, especially for the Michelin‑starred venues. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
